articles.title: Christy Carlson Romano Says She and ‘Even Stevens’ Co-Star Shia LaBeouf Were ‘Like Oil and Water’ While Filming the Disney Channel Show
articles.summary: Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the Disney Channel sitcom “Even Stevens,” is opening up about her experience working alongside co-star Shia LaBeouf. Speaking with Amanda Hirsch of the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast on Tuesday, Romano said that she and LaBeouf were “like oil and…
body: In comparison, LaBeouf has long been open about his tumultuous childhood and has said that his father was a recovering addict, and at times abusive. “He was a Venice Beach kind of bum kid,” said Romano. “It’s like that kind of vagrant fun, but also very chaotic and very scary lifestyle, and he was very young to be having that.” She likened his upbringing to the lifestyle depicted in the 1995 Larry Clark film “Kids.”
Romano did give LaBeouf credit for finding his manager at just eight years old; the “Transformers” and “Holes” star “had a dream and made it happen for himself,” she added.

“Even Stevens” ran from 2000 to 2003 and followed Ren (Romano) and Louis (LaBeouf), the two younger siblings of the Stevens family who were described as having opposing personalities and often clashing.

articles.title: Tom Cruise Pulls Out ‘Risky Business’ Dance Moves for ‘Jennifer Hudson Show’ Spirit Tunnel
articles.summary: Tom Cruise pulled out his “Risky Business” dance moves (and those black Ray-Ban sunglasses) for his much-anticipated walk down “The Jennifer Hudson Show’s” Spirit Tunnel.
body: The video, posted to social media on Tuesday, shows Cruise exit the dressing room to find “ The Jennifer Hudson Show ” staff rocking black sunglasses and singing a riff on the classic, “Old Time Rock & Roll.”

The song calls back to one of Cruise’s first movie star-making moments from the 1983 movie “Risky Business,” where he slides into frame to lip-sync and dance in his underwear and shades to Bob Seger’s version of the song.

Here, the talk show producers remix the lyrics to reference Cruise’s status as a cinema legend: “We’ve got Tom Cruise at the Happy Place. He’s in the tunnel walking to the stage,” the crew sings. “He’s a legend everybody knows. We’ve got that Tom Cruise rock and roll.”

articles.title: Patricio Guzmán obituary
articles.summary: Chilean film-maker whose trilogy on Augusto Pinochet’s coup brought him to international attention. Hawker Hunter jets bomb the presidential palace in the Chilean capital, Santiago, setting it ablaze.
body: These are the dramatic opening images of the documentary film trilogy La Batalla de Chile (The Battle of Chile), directed by Patricio Guzmán. The three films detail the struggles of the Allende government to stay in power and promote what it termed “the peaceful road to socialism”. Filmed at the time with interviews, direct footage of demonstrations, debates about how to take the Allende government forward and opposition attacks that eventually led to Pinochet’s brutal seizure of power, it had a hard-hitting immediacy that brought Guzmán a huge audience and reputation outside Chile – although the three films remained banned for many years in his own country.

While he was filming during the September 1973 coup, Guzmán, who has died aged 85, was arrested and became one of the thousands of people taken to the Estadio Nacional football stadium in Santiago, where many were arbitrarily imprisoned and tortured. He was released after a fortnight and left the country in November, first going to Spain and then Cuba, before settling in Paris, where he lived for most of the rest of his life.

articles.title: ‘Making Marie Antoinette’: A Mother’s Love Letter to Sofia Coppola’s Genius Charms NYFF
articles.summary: “I enjoyed it, but I’m never doing this again.” Sofia Coppola utters those words toward the end of “Making Marie Antoinette,” a feature documentary about the making of her 2006 film “Marie Antoinette” from her late mother, Eleanor Coppola.
body: Though Eleanor passed away in 2024 at the age of 87, she was “always frustrated that the footage was never put together [into a film],” so Sofia — with the help of editor Aaron Matthews — helped make her vision a reality. Eleanor envisioned an observational film in the vein of Frederick Wiseman, and the doc is narrated by actress Diane Lane, a longtime Coppola family collaborator, who reads Eleanor’s contemporaneous diary entries from twenty years ago. “There wasn’t much drama, so how do you make it not boring?” Sofia pondered during the Q&A.

Although there was some drama. We see Sofia and her team on “Marie Antoinette” overwhelmed at times by the amount of extras and just how long it took cast members to get their hair, makeup and costuming done (the hair, especially). In addition to a monument to Sofia, “Making Marie Antoinette” is also a celebration of the work of Milena Canonero, the film’s costume designer. Canonero created over 70 original dresses for Dunst’s Marie Antoinette alone, and eventually won the Academy Award for Best Costume Design.

articles.title: ‘What Remains’ Review: A Pensive but Stirring Drama Finds Poetry in the Landscapes of Rural Turkey
articles.summary: If you love something, let it go, the adage advises, and maybe it will come back to you. Maybe, however, it will go and go and go and never come back, and that, so Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s increasingly lyrical and persuasive “What Remains” would have it, might be its own sort of reclamation.
body: Turkish director Yeşim Ustaoğlu returns with a beautifully shot, superbly performed exploration of a modern couple embarking on separate journeys of self-discovery.

Instead she spends her days feeding the curiosity of her bright, precocious son Selim (Ali Kayra Kul), going on long walks through hilly urban Istanbul, watching over a jar of cocooning butterflies and helping him build Rube Goldberg devices in the living room of their pleasantly bohemian apartment. One room of it has recently been converted into a studio of sorts for her partner Mehmet (Metin Akdülger), an experimental musician who is as likely to want to record the sound of a malfunctioning kitchen appliance as to fix it.

articles.title: Digger review – Tom Cruise’s loudmouth oil tycoon goes hard in Alejandro G Iñárritu’s eco-satire
articles.summary: One man’s irresponsible drilling causes a global crisis in Iñárritu’s exasperatingly laborious, self-congratulatory film. A new movie from the Oscar-winning Mexican director Alejandro González Iñárritu is always an event.
body: An ageing, paunchy Texan oil tycoon called “Digger” Rockwell is seen fretfully getting up in the morning, cooing over his horrible old incontinent cat, taking urgent messages from underlings about a certain situation developing in his drilling station in the frozen Arctic. He is played by Tom Cruise with a wispy baldingness and various other prostheses, together with a good-ol’-boy twang and a Stetson borrowed from Slim Pickens’s bomb-riding army major in Kubrick’s Dr Strangelove. His prized possession is the battered old shovel his granddaddy used a century before, digging for black gold as a penniless young man in the lone star state. Digger likes to brandish this to make a point.

Digger’s – and the world’s – troubles come to a head when he is informed by his cringingly polite, querulous and terrified chief scientist Ganesh (Riz Ahmed) that the company’s irresponsible drilling practices, of which Ganesh has been warning Digger for quite some time, have caused a crisis: a vast ice floe, many times the size of Manhattan island, has broken away from the Arctic landmass and is now moving quickly towards the coast of Norway. Its imminent landfall is going to be like a nuclear attack.
points: One man’s irresponsible drilling causes a global crisis in Iñárritu’s exasperatingly laborious, self-congratulatory film.

articles.title: The Twilight Zone Creator Rod Serling Worked On A Survival Series That Could Have Been Legendary
articles.summary: After The Twilight Zone ended Rod Serling worked on a quickly canceled TV series that had plenty of potential, even though he wasn't happy with it.
body: According to Rod Serling "The Twilight Zone" is not a sci-fi series. But it doesn't really matter what you call it. The show remains the greatest TV anthology series of all time, and if it was the only thing Serling ever did he'd still be a legend. After the show was canceled in 1964, however, Serling maintained his prolific output, which at one point saw him write the pilot for a series called "The New People," which was both ahead of its time and viewed with a certain disdain by the creator himself.

After "The Twilight Zone" Serling created the short-lived Western series "The Loner," in which he tried to hook audiences by bringing his socially conscious sensibility to the small screen Oater. It didn't quite work out, and Serling moved on. Before creating his second most-famous show "Night Gallery," he penned a few TV movies, after which he lent his talents to a new show created by Aaron Spelling and Lawrence Gordon.

articles.title: Cliff Booth Officially Marks The End Of An Era For David Fincher And Netflix
articles.summary: It's been a good run for both sides, but "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" will officially wrap up David Fincher's current film deal with Netflix.
body: The last time audiences saw the character of Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) was at the end of Quentin Tarantino's alternate-history film "Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood" in 2019. In that film, Cliff works as a stuntman and general gopher for trashy TV actor Rick Dalton (Leonard DiCaprio), and it was heavily implied that he had previously, deliberately, murdered his wife. His propensity for violence often got him into trouble, as when he bested Bruce Lee in hand-to-hand combat before a film shoot. His violence, however, served him well in the film's climax when Cliff viciously murders a few Manson Family members before they could take any lives.

The results of that alternate timeline will be seen in David Fincher's upcoming film "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," which was written by Quentin Tarantino. That movie is scheduled to be released in IMAX theaters on November 26, 2026, and will make its Netflix debut on December 23.
points: It's been a good run for both sides, but "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" will officially wrap up David Fincher's current film deal with Netflix.

articles.title: Close-up look at Turner's '£50m' Rome painting on show in the city
articles.summary: Turner’s early 19th century painting - Rome, from Mount Aventine - will be on display in the Italian capital for the first time ahead of an auction in London in December.
body: A renowned painting by British landscape artist JMW Turner has returned to the city that inspired it nearly two centuries ago.
Rome, from Mount Aventine features a panoramic view of the Italian capital and will be on display at the Palazzo Rondinini for three days.
Dating back to the 19th century, the masterpiece was based on sketches made in Rome.
The work of art is remarkably well preserved and is believed to have never been restored. It even features traces of fingerprints and brush hairs are still visible.

articles.title: The Portuguese House review – picturesque, polite drama of secrets and revelations at a country estate
articles.summary: Spanish drama about people leaving their old lives behind plays out like a literary novel, with Manolo Solo excellent as a discombobulated gardener. Out of the blue, a woman walks out on her husband.
body: Manolo Solo gives an excellent performance as the left-behind husband, Fernando, an introspective mild-mannered geography professor. After his wife’s disappearance, Fernando goes on holiday to Portugal, where he meets a gardener called Manuel. When Manuel drops dead of a heart attack, Fernando decides – like his wife – to leave his old life behind; he assumes Manuel’s identity and takes a job as the gardener at a Portuguese country estate. The owner, Amália (Maria de Medeiros), senses that this intellectual man with glasses and a clumsy way with the loppers is not the man she hired, but doesn’t push it – possibly because she is attracted to him.

Like a doorstop paperback, The Portuguese House is an expansive watch, spanning years and going at a gentle pace for nearly two hours. There are more secrets and lies to come – and another person pretending to be someone they are not. That would be a twist too far in another film, but works here in a restrained drama that treats all its characters generously and with sympathy. Though in the end I wondered if it is possibly too respectful, sweeping away difficult hard-to-shift feelings like autumn leaves.

articles.title: Mary Tyler Moore’s Most Famous Fits Inspire a New Collection Benefiting Diabetes Research
articles.summary: In collaboration with Frances Valentine, the 20-piece drop includes clothing and accessories, with a portion of the profits going to help people living with the chronic condition.
body: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

Frances Valentine, the fashion brand created by the late Kate Spade and her friend Elyce Arons, is dipping into the glamorous world of old Hollywood with a new Mary Tyler Moore collection that pays homage to the actress.

The limited-edition capsule features 19 pieces, including shirts, dresses, tote bags and, of course, shoes, all inspired by the Emmy-winning star’s whimsical, upscale style. Prices start at $48 for a makeup clutch and go up to $498 for wool peacoats.
The actress was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes in the Sixties, at age 33, just as she was entering one of the most successful periods of her career.
